key_insight: SeeEEG turns EEG into images so a frozen vision foundation model outperforms specialized frozen EEG foundation models across eight datasets.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can reuse pretrained vision encoders for EEG by learning a compact signal-to-image display rather than fine-tuning the backbone.
method: Render each EEG channel in a dedicated patch row as a fixed-gain waveform or frequency-scaled scalogram.
Optimize montage, filtering, and contrast through the frozen encoder using at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view.
Pair frozen encoders with identical readout heads for comparison.
evidence_signal: Against seven EEG foundation models on eight datasets, DINOv3-based SeeEEG led balanced accuracy on all eight; random ViT-B initialization reduced scores by 15.2 points on average.
watch_item: Results establish frozen-encoder performance, not superiority over fine-tuned EEG models; display parameters still require task-specific optimization.
paper_title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
